municipal-solid-waste.def: Municipal solid waste (MSW): everyday trash from homes, schools and businesses, such as paper, food, yard waste, plastics, metals and glass. It does not include industrial, mining or farm waste.

sanitary-landfill.def: An engineered site for burying solid waste, with a clay and plastic liner, leachate collection pipes, daily soil cover, methane gas wells and a final cap, designed to keep waste, liquid and gas from escaping.

leachate.def: Liquid that forms when water seeps through buried waste and dissolves chemicals from it. Landfill liners and pipes collect it so it does not pollute groundwater.

incineration.def: Burning solid waste at high temperature. It reduces waste volume by about 90% and can generate electricity (waste-to-energy), but releases air pollutants and leaves ash that may be toxic.

e-waste.def: Discarded electronics such as phones, computers and televisions. They contain toxic metals such as lead, mercury and cadmium as well as valuable metals, so they need special recycling or disposal.
